# Independent review of ArithmeticRow254

**CLEAN mathematical/API audit.** No source edits, Lean build or replay by this reviewer.

Source `/home/codex/.codex/worktrees/ec20/Proofs/Computability/BusyBeaver/Lean/BusyBeaver/ZFC/ArithmeticRow254.lean`: SHA256 `8ed5930a5f5ce0fadba30d5247d3fa2daa732cb5433074ae46ae3d21af5edc43`,291 lines. Audit `/home/codex/.codex/worktrees/ec20/Proofs/Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/ZFC/arithmetic_row254_audit.lean`: SHA256 `c0de32721c2a61eba3b1b7d5eb5776cedfc2eda17aea6e1dbfd1f32e2a851b5a`,17 probes/37 callers. Both match the published successful maintained replay exactly.

The entire source and audit were read, together with the actual `Code254History.row`, prerequisite bounded graphs and the pinned Foundation subtraction specification.

## Proof checks

- **Exact model assumptions and predecessors** (ArithmeticRow254:15-21): Only arbitrary ORingStructure V with actual IOpen-model instance is assumed. Nonzero u is positive by zero-le and inequality; discreteness gives1<=u and truncated subtraction cancels. No standardness or external well-foundedness/induction is assumed.
- **MP graph and positivity** (ArithmeticRow254:25-44,53-61): MPGate uses predecessor witnesses x<=u,m<=v with u=x+1,v=m+1 and m=wim x a. This is exactly the encoded-child positivity/major test. The arithmetic formula bounds witnesses by child results, not rejected row output. mpDef includes both successful a+1 and failed0 branches. Arbitrary-Q predecessor_witness is only an elementary equivalence, not an object-level arbitrary-predicate induction resource.
- **GEN graph** (ArithmeticRow254:63-75): u=0 has direct result0. Otherwise the predecessor x<=u exists uniquely and f=wal a x is bounded by output r=f+1. No output-bound assertion is used on an invalid child branch.
- **Payload bounds in all models** (ArithmeticRow254:78-93,136-146,190-204): Actual Cantor bijection/projection lemmas under IOpen provide a,t,b,c<=p even for nonstandard p or a rejected row. The fourth rho8 split has components<=c<=p. All decompositions remain satisfiable when result r=0; none incorrectly bounds a positive payload by that output.
- **Foundation/core Nat subtraction bridge** (ArithmeticRow254:97-107): foundation_sub_nat identifies the explicitly chosen Foundation Arithmetic.sub on Nat with ordinary Nat truncated subtraction, through its actual unique specification. Foundation PeanoMinus/Functions.lean:25-35 defines that operation by the nonnegative-difference/zero-underflow specification; native Nat subtraction satisfies it. This prevents relying on scoped notation as if both implementations were definitionally identical.
- **Exact Nat MP/GEN adapters** (ArithmeticRow254:109-134): MPGate_nat iff gives both u!=0 and v!=0 and exact v-1=wim(u-1,a). mpValue_nat covers both zero children and a false major test. genValue_nat explicitly rewrites Foundation subtraction to native Nat subtraction; all input values, not only valid derivations, are included.
- **Literal complete row formula** (ArithmeticRow254:148-188): rowKernel and the literal Sigma0 rowDef have identical output-first argument order r,k,p,u,v and all twelve branches plus default. Pair/constructor calls expand previously defined bounded ring-language formulas. Successful formula results are encoded f+1, allowing f<=r; failed gates use direct output0 without requiring construction of an output-bounded bundle.
- **Generic definedness proof** (ArithmeticRow254:206-240): row_defined proves the actual fixed formula evaluates iff output equals rowKernel for every Fin5 assignment in every IOpen model. Pair-projection elimination is justified by payload bounds. The finite12-way case split is exhaustive in any such model, with a default for values unequal to all twelve numerals, not merely externally standard tags.
- **All-Nat live row adapter** (ArithmeticRow254:242-288): rowKernel_nat matches actual Code254History.row for every rec:Nat->Nat,tag,payload. GEN uses rec tail as first child, MP uses rec b and rec c, and other rows ignore children. Cases0..11 plus n+12 cover all tags. rowEnv supplies output/tag/payload/those two values; rowGraph_nat combines generic definedness with the exact live-row equality.
- **Proof boundary** (ArithmeticRow254:header,242-280): A graph of one row with two explicit child-result inputs is obtained. rec is an arbitrary external function used to select values for rowEnv. Neither an object-language oracle nor a represented history lookup is asserted; rec need not even be valid proof history. The full outer code0/positive base12 selector, course-of-values history, PA totality and effective finite proof translations remain separate.

## Rule-by-rule comparison

| Tag | Decoded payload | Row result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `p` | `if p=0 then1 else0` |
| 1 | `P(a,P(b,c))` | `mpValue a u v` |
| 2 | `P(a,tail)` | `genValue a u` |
| 3 | `P(a,tail)` | `rho1 a tail+1` |
| 4 | `P(a,P(b,c))` | `rho2 a b c+1` |
| 5 | `P(a,P(b,c))` | `rho3 a b c+1` |
| 6 | `P(a,P(b,c))` | `rho4 a b c+1` |
| 7 | `P(a,P(b,c))` | `rho5 a b c+1` |
| 8 | `P(a,tail)` | `rho6 a tail+1` |
| 9 | `P(a,P(b,c))` | `rho7 a b c+1` |
| 10 | `P(a,P(b,P(d,e)))` | `rho8 a b d e+1` |
| 11 | `P(a,P(b,c))` | `if c!=a and c!=b then bundle a b c+1 else0` |
| all other internal k | `any` | `0` |

Both original bundle inequalities are retained. A successful conclusion of formula-code0 is encoded1; invalid data is encoded0. Outer proof-code0 remains invalid in `Code254History.step`, outside this row-only graph. The default applies to every other internal tag and to every natural tag>=12 in the standard adapter.

## Audit and exact boundary

The stored audit includes generic IOpen definedness callers, arbitrary child-result adapters, each of12 tags, invalid tags12/12345, zero-child MP/GEN, successful formula0, false major shape and both failed bundle gates at arbitrary payload size. The function `rec` supplies explicit values; no represented oracle/history lookup is hidden in the graph. import BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254
open LO LO.FirstOrder LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic
open scoped LO.FirstOrder.Arithmetic
open SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC
open ArithmeticCantor ArithmeticRow254
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.pred_add_one
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.pred_le
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.mpGate_defined
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.mp_defined
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.bounded_succ_iff
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.predecessor_witness
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.gen_defined
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.payload_fields
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.foundation_sub_nat
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.mpGate_nat
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.mpValue_nat
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.genValue_nat
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.pair_fields
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.payload_fields_flat
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.row_defined
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.rowKernel_nat
#print axioms SetTheory.BusyBeaver.ZFC.ArithmeticRow254.rowGraph_nat
section Generic
variable {V : Type*} [ORingStructure V] [V↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧* 𝗜𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻]
example (e : Fin 3 → V) : mpGateDef.val.Evalb e ↔ MPGate (e 0) (e 1) (e 2) := mpGate_defined.df e
example (e : Fin 4 → V) : mpDef.val.Evalb e ↔ e 0 = mpValue (e 1) (e 2) (e 3) := mp_defined.df e
example (e : Fin 3 → V) : genDef.val.Evalb e ↔ e 0 = genValue (e 1) (e 2) := gen_defined.df e
example (e : Fin 5 → V) : rowDef.val.Evalb e ↔ e 0 = rowKernel (e 1) (e 2) (e 3) (e 4) := row_defined.df e
example (u : V) : u - 1 ≤ u := pred_le u
example (u : V) (hu : u ≠ 0) : u - 1 + 1 = u := pred_add_one u hu
example (p : V) (Q : V → V → V → V → Prop) :
    (∃ a, a ≤ p ∧ ∃ t, t ≤ p ∧ p = cantor a t ∧ ∃ b, b ≤ p ∧ ∃ c, c ≤ p ∧ t = cantor b c ∧ Q a t b c) ↔
    Q (first p) (second p) (first (second p)) (second (second p)) := payload_fields p Q
example (p bound : V) (hp : p ≤ bound) (Q : V → V → Prop) :
    (∃ a, a ≤ bound ∧ ∃ b, b ≤ bound ∧ p = cantor a b ∧ Q a b) ↔ Q (first p) (second p) := pair_fields p bound hp Q
example (p u v : V) : rowKernel 12 p u v = 0 := by simp [rowKernel]
example (a v : V) : mpValue a 0 v = 0 := by simp [mpValue, MPGate]
end Generic
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (tag p : Nat) :
    rowKernel tag p (if tag = 2 then rec (SetTheory.Cantor.ofNat p).2 else rec (SetTheory.Cantor.ofNat (SetTheory.Cantor.ofNat p).2).1)
      (rec (SetTheory.Cantor.ofNat (SetTheory.Cantor.ofNat p).2).2) = Code254History.row rec tag p := rowKernel_nat rec tag p
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (tag p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec tag p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec tag p := rowGraph_nat rec tag p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 0 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 0 p := rowGraph_nat rec 0 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 1 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 1 p := rowGraph_nat rec 1 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 2 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 2 p := rowGraph_nat rec 2 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 3 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 3 p := rowGraph_nat rec 3 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 4 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 4 p := rowGraph_nat rec 4 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 5 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 5 p := rowGraph_nat rec 5 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 6 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 6 p := rowGraph_nat rec 6 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 7 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 7 p := rowGraph_nat rec 7 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 8 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 8 p := rowGraph_nat rec 8 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 9 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 9 p := rowGraph_nat rec 9 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 10 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 10 p := rowGraph_nat rec 10 p out
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p out : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 11 p out) ↔ out = Code254History.row rec 11 p := rowGraph_nat rec 11 p out
-- Successful code0 remains encoded as value1; invalid is value0.
example (u v : Nat) : rowKernel 0 0 u v = 1 := by simp [rowKernel]
example (p u v : Nat) (hp : p ≠ 0) : rowKernel 0 p u v = 0 := by simp [rowKernel, hp]
example (p u v : Nat) : rowKernel 12 p u v = 0 := by simp [rowKernel]
example (p u v : Nat) : rowKernel 12345 p u v = 0 := by simp [rowKernel]
example (a v : Nat) : mpValue a 0 v = 0 := by simp
example (a u : Nat) : mpValue a u 0 = 0 := by simp
example : mpValue (0 : Nat) 1 1 = 1 := by simp [Code254.wim, Code254.P, SetTheory.Cantor.toNat, SetTheory.Cantor.tri]
example : mpValue (1 : Nat) 1 1 = 0 := by simp [Code254.wim, Code254.P, SetTheory.Cantor.toNat, SetTheory.Cantor.tri]
example (a : Nat) : genValue a 0 = 0 := by simp
example (a : Nat) : genValue a 1 = Code254.wal a 0 + 1 := by simp
-- Each failed bundle gate has a valid output0 graph even at arbitrary payload size.
example (a b u v : Nat) : rowKernel 11 (cantor a (cantor b a)) u v = 0 := by
  simp only [rowKernel, first_cantor, second_cantor]
  simp
example (a b u v : Nat) : rowKernel 11 (cantor a (cantor b b)) u v = 0 := by
  simp only [rowKernel, first_cantor, second_cantor]
  simp
example (rec : Nat → Nat) (p : Nat) : rowDef.val.Evalb (rowEnv rec 12 p 0) :=
  (rowGraph_nat rec 12 p 0).mpr (by simp [Code254History.row])
